svg.title: Front view muscle chart. Primary muscles: Glutes, Quads. Secondary muscles: Abs, Hamstrings, Adductors, Calves.
Back view muscle chart. Primary muscles: Glutes, Quads. Secondary muscles: Abs, Hamstrings, Adductors, Calves.

svg.text: It drives a heavy bar through the deepest loaded knee and hip range of anything here, and a barbell is the easiest
thing in the gym to add a little more weight to each week.
Taking too short a step — the front knee travels well past the toes and the joint absorbs the load the glutes
Letting the front knee wobble inward on the drive up — the glute is not controlling the femur and the knee tracks
Leaning the torso out over the front thigh — the lower back rounds under the dumbbells and the glute loses its line
Hold dumbbells at your sides, torso tall. Step forward and drop your back
knee toward the floor. Drive through the front heel to step into the next
Breathing — Inhale as the back knee lowers toward the floor and exhale as you
drive through the front heel to stand.

dumbbells; balance failures, not muscle failures, are what turn lunges into
Shorten the depth or hold a static split squat instead if a knee issue

Best on paper is not always best for you. Which exercise builds a body part fastest depends on your build, your injury history and how much of the movement you already own — someone who cannot yet hold

a flat back under load will get more from the exercise ranked third than from the one ranked first. Treat this as a starting point for a conversation, not a verdict: ask a coach on the floor before you
